summary: @servicetitan/titan-chatbot-api preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated 727KB payload
details: package.json declares preinstall=`node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs is obfuscated with `_0x...` identifiers and, on `npm install`, checks for a local `bun` binary; if absent, it constructs a URL against github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, downloads a Bun zip at a pinned version, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, then runs `execFileSync(bunPath, [path.join(D, 'math_init.js')], { stdio: 'inherit' })`. The sibling `math_init.js` at the tarball root is a 727KB heavily obfuscated blob using a string-array rotator (`WV8StW`/`n7gIxM`) with hex-mangled identifiers and a decoder function (`hc1jfK9`), is not referenced by `dist/index.js`, and is not documented in README or CHANGELOG. The package advertises itself as a TypeScript chatbot API client, a purpose that does not require fetching a second language runtime or executing a large obfuscated blob at install time. Invoking the payload through a freshly downloaded Bun runtime rather than Node evades scanners that only inspect Node-resolved code. Additional static evidence in dist/api-client/titan-chat/native-client.js shows `ping` alongside multiple `POST` sites consistent with outbound network activity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
